totalByProduct(): adds up OrderLine quantities per productId; this is pure domain calculation

parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/domain/stock-reservation-service.ts is a domain service, and every responsibility it has is domain logic. In `totalByProduct` it adds up quantities per product. `reserve` applies the all-or-none rule: it checks `canReserve` for every product before changing any of them. `release` gives stock back. It throws domain errors (NotFoundError, InsufficientStockError). To load and store products it uses ProductRepository, an interface (a "port") defined in the domain layer. It never touches a concrete database, ORM, SQL, HTTP, framework or transport code. Calling an abstract repository port from a domain service is a normal DDD pattern, so this is not persistence logic sitting in the wrong layer. There is one judgment call: the load-then-save sequence could arguably live in the application layer. But it goes only through the domain abstraction and supports a rule that spans several products, so I don't count it as misplaced. No ADR text was provided, so there was nothing extra to check against.
